events.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
events.description: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains. Continue reading...
events.ticker_label: 🌪️ California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state

events.title: Australian politics live: Labor to ‘save more than we spend’ in budget update, Chalmers says; rental affordability plummets to 14-year low
events.description: Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The government will save more than it spends, says Jim Chalmers , but it won’t be a “slash and burn” budget update. Unlike the federal budget, where we get plenty of notice of when it will be handed down, the government only gives us a few days notice for the mid-financial year economic and fiscal outlook (or Myefo). There’s still a fair bit of work to do to finalise it all, but we’ve made enough progress to be confident that at this stage there will be a modest net save in the budget. We’re not going to slash and burn in the budget where that would impact the payments that people receive or where it would impact some of the more sensitive parts of the economy. But we haven’t focused the savings on just one portfolio. There will be a number of savings in the mid-year update. They will be substantial, as I said. These are serious times. You can see in the quite extraordinary reaction on the stock market just how volatile global markets are right now. I think it’s a bit of a symbol of the quite extraordinary volatility, unpredictability that we’re seeing play out in markets in the AI sector, but more broadly as well. Continue reading...

events.title: Democrats win House by largest margin in 50 years. And, COP31 ends with no deal
events.description: Democrats have currently flipped 47 House seats and could flip 49 total. And, climate change talks at COP31 ran two days longer than expected, becoming the longest conference in the summit's history.

events.title: What did Xi Jinping get from the bear hug with Trump at the Shenzhen summit?
events.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Robert Daly, director of the program on US China relations at University of Maryland's School of Public Policy, about President Trump's trip to China this week.

events.title: Highlights and challenges from covering an historic month in South America
events.description: NPR's South America Correspondent discusses her work covering an historic election upset and a papal visit.

events.title: Denmark: Top court backs hardline immigration "ghetto law"
events.description: Denmark's Supreme Court has found that evictions of "non-Western" residents do not amount to discrimination. The government in Copenhagen argues its "ghetto law" encourages integration.

events.title: North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate
events.description: EU enlargement has regained momentum, with Montenegro and Albania moving closer to membership. But North Macedonia, a candidate since 2005, remains stalled by a politically difficult dispute involving Bulgaria.

events.title: COP deadlock prompts calls for a reset of climate diplomacy
events.description: COP31 has been branded a failure after countries couldn't reach a final agreement, divided over a reference to "fossil fuels." But was the decision to walk away from a watered-down text actually a show of strength?

events.title: 'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract
events.description: For decades, Germans have known Hollywood's biggest stars through the same familiar voices. Now an AI clause in Netflix contracts is splitting the industry over whether it protects performers or exposes them.

events.title: NATO Parliamentary Assembly convenes amid Russian airspace violations
events.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and German Foreign Minister Wadephul are set to address the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin while NATO representatives discuss Russian airspace violations in Brussels. DW has more.

events.title: Rule-breaking is contagious — and good examples barely help
events.description: Seeing someone break a rule makes people more likely to break it too, a new study finds, especially when the rule-breaker is on their side politically. Watching others behave well barely made a difference.

events.description: No description available.

events.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar plans to visit Ukraine soon, signaling improved relations between the two countries

events.description: Greece’s oldest modern-era museum has reopened on the Acropolis in Athens after a seven-year, 6.2 million-euro ($6.8 million) restoration

events.description: British police have evacuated over 12,000 fans from a Don Toliver concert after an unknown substance was released in the crowd

events.title: Thai court upholds royal defamation conviction for opposition lawmaker and cuts sentence to 3 years
events.description: An appeals court has upheld the conviction of an opposition lawmaker for defaming Thailand’s monarchy in social media posts but reduced her prison sentence from six years to three

events.title: Carney enlists fake Trump for laughs at Canada's annual press gallery dinner
events.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney shared the stage with a fake Donald Trump and two versions of himself Saturday, enlisting comedians to help roast the U.S. president and Canadian politicians at an annual dinner with journalists

events.title: Guterres laments COP31 outcome, urges climate justice from Barbados
events.description: Secretary-General António Guterres on Sunday expressed deep disappointment over the collapse of COP31 climate negotiations, using a visit to Barbados to call for stronger action on fossil fuels, climate finance and support for vulnerable nations.

events.title: ‘I had a better life in Iran’: Afghan women forced home struggle to rebuild
events.description: For five years, Zahra cared for an elderly woman in Iran and earned enough to get by. Now back in Herat, western Afghanistan, the 28-year-old trained midwife is unemployed. She lives with her parents and siblings, apart from her six-year-old son, who lives with her ex-husband.

events.title: Shattered playgrounds and freezing classrooms: Inside Ukraine’s deadliest year for children
events.description: Amid the ruins of a twice-bombed Kyiv kindergarten as a day-long power cut continued, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) on Friday highlighted the dangers to youngsters enduring another brutal winter in Ukraine, as child casualty numbers rise to record levels.
events.ticker_label: 💥 Shattered playgrounds and freezing classrooms: Inside Ukraine’s deadliest year for children

events.title: Peacekeeping: With 500 paternity and child support claims unresolved, UN scales up accountability
events.description: The UN is adding new accountability measures to better support children fathered by peacekeepers, the Under-Secretary-General for Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance, Catherine Pollard, announced Thursday.

events.title: Rush hour road rage suspect’s bail revoked as slain utility worker’s supporters shout at accused murderer
events.description: Retired NYPD officer Victor Romero, accused of killing Con Edison worker Koran Irvine on the George Washington Bridge, had his $1 million bond revoked.

events.title: Louisiana man accused of random nature trail murder, killing coworker with crossbow days later
events.description: Jared Schurr allegedly strangled Lizeht Rodriguez at Northlake Nature Center before killing coworker Woodrow Scott with a crossbow, officials say.

events.title: Man convicted for role in Tessa Majors' 2019 NYC killing released on parole
events.description: Luchiano Lewis, convicted in the 2019 murder of Barnard College freshman Tessa Majors, was freed on conditional parole after serving fewer than seven years behind bars.

events.title: Mississippi mother, caregiver face charges after refusing to give cancer treatment to toddler
events.description: Destiny Schliefert faces felony murder charges after police say she refused cancer treatment for her 3-year-old son, who weighed 24 pounds when he died.
events.ticker_label: 💥 Mississippi mother, caregiver face charges after refusing to give cancer treatment to toddler

events.title: Harvard scientist may never prove mysterious space object’s origin after mission scrapped
events.description: Avi Loeb claims JAXA's canceled Hayabusa2 landing mission on 1998 KY26 ends the only chance to prove the object is the lost Soviet probe Phobos 1.

events.title: Biotech CEO says the US is fighting fentanyl ‘all wrong,’ urges new Democratic Congress to step up
events.description: Nearly a year after President Donald Trump designated illicit fentanyl a weapon of mass destruction, ARMR Sciences' CEO says treat it like a bioweapon.

events.title: Captain who abandoned passengers on sinking Costa Concordia cruise ship released early from prison
events.description: Costa Concordia captain Francesco Schettino is out of a Rome prison after 9 years, set to serve the remaining 7 years on supervised probation, lawyer says.

events.title: Trump says Iran unleashed missile, drone surge after midterms
events.description: President Donald Trump says Iran launched more missiles and drones over the past week than at any point in over a year, and all were knocked down with no damage.

events.title: Flavio Bolsonaro claims judge ordered passports seized just 7 minutes after Brazil election loss
events.description: Former presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro alleges election interference by Brazil’s Supreme Court and discusses political persecution and the future of his family’s political movement.

events.title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to kill Ukrainian American rapper on Danish soil
events.description: Denmark's PET accuses Russia of an assassination plot against Kyivstoner, expelling Moscow's defense attache as two gang-affiliated men plead guilty.

events.title: FBI Ten Most Wanted cartel leader 'Chapo Isidro' captured by Mexico's 'elite military forces' after US help
events.description: FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, who goes by the alias "Chapo Isidro," was captured in Guasave, Mexico, sparking a gun battle.
